findings.problem: status is a bare pub String, allowing any arbitrary string value (e.g. "deleted", "pending", "") as a valid budget workflow status.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can set item.status to an invalid lifecycle value, breaking workflow invariants at runtime with no compile-time enforcement.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a `pub status: BudgetStatus` enum with explicit variants (e.g. `Pending`, `Validated`, `Sent`). Make the field non-pub or provide a fallible constructor that only allows valid transitions.

findings.problem: is_validated is a bare pub bool — a boolean cannot express the directionality or ordering of a lifecycle transition.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can flip is_validated from true to false, creating an illegal reversed transition. The bool provides no information about whether validation was required or what state precedes/follows it.
findings.fix: Replace `pub is_validated: bool` with an enum or typestate (e.g. `validation: ValidationState` with `Unvalidated`, `Validated`), or remove the flag entirely and encode validation as a typestate parameter on BudgetWorkflow.

findings.problem: is_sent is a bare pub bool — same lifecycle-flag anti-pattern as is_validated.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set is_sent to true without going through mark_sent, or set it to false after marking sent. The bool carries no transition ordering guarantees.
findings.fix: Replace `pub is_sent: bool` with an enum or typestate (e.g. `sent: SentState` with `NotSent`, `Sent`), or remove it entirely since status="Sent" already conveys the state once status is an enum.

findings.problem: id is a bare pub String with no domain newtype. There is no validation that the id has the expected format, length, or prefix.
findings.failure_mode: Any invalid string (empty, malformed, wrong prefix) can be stored as a budget workflow id. The core has no invariant enforcement — errors are discovered downstream rather than at the parse boundary.
findings.fix: Define a `BudgetId` newtype struct with a private inner String field and a `try_from` constructor that validates format/length. Replace `pub id: String` with `pub id: BudgetId` (non-pub inner).

findings.problem: mark_sent is a free function that mutates struct fields in-place rather than returning a new pure value. It is not a pure calculation — it performs field writes (implicit mutation) and heap allocation via `.to_string()`.
findings.failure_mode: The function mutates the caller-owned BudgetWorkflow, so callers cannot reason about immutability. The `.to_string()` allocation is a side effect in what should be a pure core function. No preconditions are checked (e.g. can you mark a "deleted" budget as sent?).
findings.fix: Rewrite as a pure function on an immutable reference: `fn mark_sent(item: &BudgetWorkflow) -> Result<BudgetWorkflow, BudgetError>` that returns a new BudgetWorkflow with validated transitions. Validate preconditions (status must allow transition to sent) before constructing the new value.

findings.problem: `item.status = "sent".to_string()` performs an unbounded heap allocation inside a core function instead of using a zero-copy enum variant or &'static str.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary allocation in hot-path core logic. If status is an enum, the variant is zero-cost at runtime with no heap allocation.
findings.fix: Replace String status with a `BudgetStatus` enum. The transition `item.status = BudgetStatus::Sent` is zero-allocation.

findings.problem: All fields of BudgetWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to construct arbitrary illegal states directly (e.g. status="", is_validated=true, is_sent=true, sent_at_epoch_ms=None).
findings.failure_mode: External callers can bypass any intended workflow invariants by directly setting fields, making the type untrustworthy.
findings.fix: Make all fields private (remove `pub`). Provide a fallible constructor `BudgetWorkflow::try_new(...)` that enforces invariants, and expose only read-only getters or a builder for controlled construction.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is a bare Option<u64> with no domain semantics. Any u64 is valid, including nonsensical timestamps.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can set sent_at_epoch_ms to 0, u64::MAX, or any arbitrary value with no semantic meaning. No validation that the timestamp is in a reasonable range.
findings.fix: Replace with a `sent_at: Option<EpochMillis>` newtype that wraps u64 with a validated constructor (e.g. rejects 0, enforces reasonable range). Make the inner value non-pub.

findings.problem: mark_sent does not validate any preconditions — it will set status to "sent" and is_sent to true regardless of the current status, is_validated, or is_sent state.
findings.failure_mode: Calling mark_sent on an already-sent budget, a deleted budget, or a non-validated budget silently succeeds, corrupting the workflow state machine.
findings.fix: Add precondition checks: return `Err(BudgetError::InvalidTransition)` if current status is not in a state that allows transition to sent. Check is_validated is true before allowing sent.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for any performance claim on BudgetWorkflow or mark_sent
no profiler data (flamegraph, cachegrind) for allocation hot paths
no allocation tracing (e.g. alloc_counter, dhat-rs) proving zero-allocation transition on enum-based status
no second-ring analysis (e.g. MIRI, Miri, or borrow-checker proof) for mutation safety
no command-level evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run. The crate has fundamental typestate violations: all fields are public primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) that make every illegal state representable. No enum-based status, no typestate on lifecycle, no domain newtypes for id or timestamp, no transition validation, and the sole function mutates in-place with heap allocation. These are architectural blockers that cannot be patched with local fixes; the struct and function signatures require redesign.
